$description: Platform vocabulary. A platform is the runtime whose conventions and accessibility sources apply to a component; a technology (Flutter, React Native, Qt, JavaFX, a web framework) targets one or several platforms and consumes that platform's resolved tokens, one tree per mode (platforms/<id>/<mode>.tokens.json). Every artifact is agnostic by default; a `platforms` array on a state, an example, a keyboard entry or a guideline scopes it to the listed platforms, and a `### <Name>` sub-heading scopes a paragraph of the docs. Ids must equal the `platform` enum of specs/schema/component.schema.json and the keys of `implementations` and of `platforms` in tokens/config.json.

web.name: Web
web.description: Browsers on any device, framework or not. The reference implementation in web/ targets it and the site renders it.

ios.name: iOS
ios.description: iOS and iPadOS apps. Touch first; pointer and keyboard exist (trackpad, Full Keyboard Access).

android.name: Android
android.description: Android apps. Touch first; pointer and keyboard exist (mouse, stylus, hardware keyboard).

desktop.name: Desktop
desktop.description: Native desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux. Pointer and keyboard; no touch assumed. No platform token overlay: the base values apply.

inputs.pointer: A pointing device that can hover: mouse, trackpad, stylus.
inputs.touch: Direct touch; no hover, coarse targets.
inputs.keyboard: Physical or assistive keyboard; focus moves between controls.
